Proposition
[The Gram--Schmidt Recursion: Simultaneous Induction]

↗ def:gram-schmidt-bilin ↗ lem:gram-schmidt-bilin-orthogonal-earlier ↗ lem:nondegenerate-symmetric-bilinear

Let $B$ be symmetric and $(v_1,\ldots ,v_n)$ nondegenerate. For $u=\mathrm{GS}_B(v)$ and every $k\leq n$:

  1. $B(u_i,u_i) e 0$ for every $i\leq k$;

  2. $B(u_i,u_{i'})=0$ for distinct $i,i'\leq k$;

  3. $\operatorname {span}(u_1,\ldots ,u_j)= \operatorname {span}(v_1,\ldots ,v_j)$ for every $j\leq k$.

Proof

↗ def:gram-schmidt-bilin ↗ lem:gram-schmidt-bilin-orthogonal-earlier ↗ lem:nondegenerate-symmetric-bilinear \sketch Induct on $k$. For $j=k+1$, the preceding lemma makes $u_j$ orthogonal to $S=\operatorname {span}(u_1,\ldots ,u_k)$. The recursion gives $u_j=v_j-\sigma $ for some $\sigma \in S$, so adjoining $u_j$ or $v_j$ produces the same next prefix $T$. Nondegeneracy of the input flag gives $v_j otin S$, hence $u_j e 0$. If $B(u_j,u_j)=0$, then $u_j$ is orthogonal to every vector in $T=S+\operatorname {span}(u_j)$, contradicting nondegeneracy of $T$. This proves the new denominator condition, orthogonality, and span identity simultaneously.

□
